identity recovery, status refresh and readiness controls

Implement identity recovery, status refresh and readiness controls. Keep legacy identity promotion retryable after a transient write fails without repeatedly opening the account menu or trusting unverified cached data. Coalesce status refresh across content-script instances for each shared-state revision while retaining stale-revision guards and prompt UI refresh. Distinguish identity-change pause with a held claim from an explicit pending or failed Stop so the controls offer a valid recovery action without executing work under a mismatched viewer. Update the single late-initialization hook with the latest timed-out route and schedule at most one current-document recovery. Assert actionable recovery for the first, valid Stop state for the second, and no work under the changed identity. #107: Time out on A then B, settle initialization once amid repeated focus/pageshow events, and assert exactly one recovery probe for B. Bring the published API contract and client guide into line with existing behavior

Bring the published API contract and client guide into line with existing behavior. Coordinate one writer for generated files. Inspect current parsers and handlers, use synthetic examples and the repository's generator, then check the served artifact and run the documented drift check twice. Cover each of these cases in focused contract tests:
* A single saved definition can be absent or use either supported persisted version. Both versions round-trip.
* Each export source accepts its own ID and filter choices unambiguously. A choice from the other source fails validation.
* A fresh inbox observation and a replay have their distinct success statuses and the same typed decision-object envelope. Validate real-shaped fixture responses for both statuses.
* The market intake accepts bounded free-text field names. Known names work, and an unrecognized synthetic name reaches the existing warning path.
* A validator failure from a route with an incomplete error enumeration validates under the fallback contract. Keep verified per-route error sets precise.
* The sign-in guide advertises HTML. Normal registration can omit its display name and receives the default. Derive allowable grants, response types, their combinations and required redirect metadata from the current registration parser. The guide and agent instructions explain which registered grants permit device login and later renewal. Use mock registration and a preapproved synthetic device fixture to verify documented metadata, with and without the renewal grant. Preserve existing approval and token behavior.
* The entitlement decision request mirrors the strict versioned runtime input. Validate a full decision with ID, enabled flag, revision and reason, and show that an extra idempotency field fails.
* Publish the browser operation claim and action-only completion contracts, including required dispatch identity for acceptance and rejection. Check the status, claim, execute and complete descriptions against offline fixture results.
* Session subject-derived identifiers accept a bounded opaque subject in both account and connection projections. Genuine UUID entity fields retain their format.
* A selector option accepts a null or bounded nonempty structural fragment. Verify boundary handling for match counts 0 and 10,000 and refusal of out-of-range counts. Use synthetic markup.
Record per-case passes or blocked checks. Regenerate outputs from their source and preserve independent catalog changes already present on the base.
